display.title: Episode 9: The Ten Wedding Gifts, Chapter 3 (Yud Shevat)
display.summary_short: On the eve of Yud Shevat, Uncle Yossi tells of the Frierdiker Rebbe's dangerous work teaching Torah to children, and in chapter 3 a lost child knocks on the newlyweds' door in a blizzard.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the ninth of Shevat 5742. After a clap-along niggun, Uncle Yossi opens the Hebrew calendar: tomorrow is Yud Shevat, the day the Frierdiker Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, passed away 32 years earlier, in 5710. He founded schools where children learned Torah in hiding in a land where it was forbidden, was arrested and sentenced to death, and was saved by a miracle, freed on his birthday, Yud-Beis Tammuz 5687. Mentioning a tzaddik's name brings blessing; we should be inspired to spread Torah and thank Hashem for the freedom to keep mitzvos. A young club member leads the Shema. In chapter 3 of "The Ten Wedding Gifts", Avraham and Sarah are settled in their own cottage, still puzzled by the gifts, when on a stormy winter night a lost, freezing boy knocks at the door. They warm him by the fire and put him to bed, planning to take him home to his worried parents when the storm ends. What happens there is saved for next week. In the mailbox, a mother asks whether her little daughter may talk to Uncle Yossi on the phone.
display.lesson: Learn from the lives of tzaddikim to spread Torah and mitzvos, and be kind to anyone in need; Hashem arranges events to reward kindness.
